locator.text: Equation (8.7), p. 90, in the statement of Lemma 8.2

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has a weaker form of it. The formula itself is stated literally, but only for two of the paper's three values of e. Lemma 8.2 fixes e ∈ {0,1,2} and (8.6) defines D_e = D_r + e/R, T_e f = R^{-e} I_c(R^e f), A_e f = R^{-e}(∂_R χ_m) J(R^e f). Lean states D_e T_e f = f − A_e f with the literal cutoff remainder at e = 0 (compactPrimitive_radial_identity, physicalGraphDeriv_physicalCompact_global, transport_compact_eq_sub_alias, and UniformFourierAlias.lean:152) and at e = 1 (streamGamma_eq_desired_sub_alias, and PhysicalMeanDomain.lean:1605). I found no declaration stating it at e = 2: a repository-wide search of NavierStokes/ for a right-hand side of the form `… - (compactAlias|physicalAlias|cutoffAlias|exactAlias) …` returns exactly those seven lines, all e = 0 or e = 1. The paper does use the e = 2 case, in Corollary 8.5 (p. 95), where (D_r + 2/R)H_θ = −⟨E_θ⟩_Y + σ_θ ε∂_Z J_θ; there the source is independent of Y and has zero weighted radial integral, so by Lemma 8.2's last sentence the cutoff remainder vanishes. That degenerate case is covered in Lean by a different operator: SignedStressPrimitive.sigma P e F = −R^{-e} I_c(R^e F) (line 164) with a bump-density correction subtracted instead of the χ_m cutoff remainder, and physical_weighted_sigma_hasDerivAt gives (D_r + e/R)σ = −(F − bump) for every e, specialized at e = 2 by physical_angular_divergence (line 821, radialDivergence 2 σ = −adjusted; IntegratedMeanBalances.radialDivergence c f r = f'(r) + (c/r)f(r)). So the shortfall is the general-A_e form of (8.7) at e = 2, which is not used by the paper; the e = 0 and e = 1 statements are term-for-term the paper's, including the R^{-e} normalization and the (∂_R χ_m)·J shape of A_e.
